correction: Added schematic of I_0 through I_10, the included endpoint (1,0), and the disjoint closed vertical segment added by closure. All prior title, statement, hypotheses, proof, dependencies, sources, verification and status bytes remain unchanged.

diagram_math_checks.objects: f:(0,1] -> [0,1], G={(x,f(x))}, and added segment {0} x [0,1]
diagram_math_checks.check: The domain excludes x=0, so the orange segment is disjoint from G. Statement claim 2 and proof steps 3.2/4.2 identify exactly this segment as the closure addition. No drawn blue segment meets x=0.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Twelve vertices, eleven consecutive affine pieces
diagram_math_checks.check: For n=0,...,11 the x coordinates approximate 1/(n+1) to six decimals where needed; heights alternate 0,1 beginning at (1,0), as the defining epsilon_n requires. Consecutive vertices give I_0,...,I_10. At x=1/2 the height is 1, matching epsilon_1. The figure is geometric and unoriented; it asserts no morphisms or commutativity.

The final displayed vertex is approximately (1/12,1). Caption explicitly omits I_n for n>=11; dots are an omission symbol, not an extra curve, endpoint or bridge. Step 1.5 gives oscillations arbitrarily close to zero, and step 3.2 gives accumulation at every height, rather than only the endpoints.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Closed segment and included graph endpoint
diagram_math_checks.check: Filled markers at (0,0),(0,1) represent included endpoints of {0} x [0,1], and the filled blue marker at (1,0) represents f(1)=0 in G. No open endpoint ring is asserted. The rigorous connectivity and non-path-connectivity proof is unchanged and independent of the illustration.
